title: Implement organization create and read API
acceptance_criteria: A new tenant can be created and read over HTTP; operations are OIDC-authorized and tenant-scoped; product-neutral.
required_tests: API integration tests plus negative foreign-tenant and unauthorized-role tests
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL. api_routes.csv rows GET/POST /api/v1/organizations exist but no endpoint is mapped (Organizations module has repos/resolver only). Add OrganizationEndpoints under a RequireAuthorization group following the WorkspaceEndpoints.cs pattern. Reuse Organization aggregate + OrganizationRepository + the OIDC principal/tenant resolvers. Creating an org makes the caller its Owner via OrganizationMember. Fail-closed; hidden-404 for foreign tenants. No new tables.

title: Implement current-principal endpoint GET api/v1/me
acceptance_criteria: An authenticated caller can read their principal context (user profile + org memberships + roles); anonymous callers get 401.
required_tests: Integration tests for authenticated read and 401 for anonymous
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL. api_routes.csv row GET /api/v1/me not implemented (only UserProfileReferenceService exists). Project the mapped principal (OidcPrincipalMapper) + memberships into a safe DTO. No secrets/tokens in the response (T7). Reuse TenantContextResolver/membership lookups; do not expose other tenants.

title: Implement session create and list API
acceptance_criteria: A host can create a session in a workspace and list a workspace's sessions over HTTP; start/end then operate on a real created session; session.active.max quota enforced on create.
required_tests: Lifecycle + authorization negative tests; quota-exceeded test
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL. SessionEndpoints.cs maps only /{sessionId}/start and /end - there is NO create or list route, so sessions are unreachable via API. Add POST and GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/sessions. Resolve workspace via workspace-scoped lookup first, authorize host roles, enforce session.active.max via the existing quota services, then create the Session aggregate. Emit nothing here unless CORE-EVT-001 has landed (events are a separate story). Fail-closed; hidden-404.

title: Make VisibilityPreviewService participant-aware
acceptance_criteria: GetVisibleResources takes a participantId and returns exactly the resources that participant may see including selected-participant private reveals; audience-wide and private reveals both handled; fail-closed.
required_tests: Unit tests: audience-wide visible, private reveal visible only to the selected participant, hidden invisible, foreign-tenant empty
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL (shared primitive for the feed + search retrofits). apps/api/Visibility/VisibilityPreviewService.cs is currently audience-wide only and has zero callers (dead code). Retrofit it to accept participantId and delegate per-candidate to VisibilityPolicy.CanParticipantViewResourceAsync (the participant-aware primitive already used by EventRecipientVisibility). DO NOT duplicate visibility logic - reuse VisibilityPolicy. This is the single source the feed (API-005) and entity search (API-006) will consume.

title: Implement the real participant visible-feed projection
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/participants/{participantId}/visible-feed returns the participant's actually-visible scenes/content/entities; a participant never sees content not revealed to them or revealed only to another participant.
required_tests: Integration tests incl. the crown-jewel: a participant does NOT see another participant's private reveal; foreign-tenant 404; unowned participantId 404
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL - THE core participant feature. apps/api/Visibility/VisibilityEndpoints.cs returns ParticipantVisibleFeedResponse.Empty unconditionally and ParticipantVisibleFeedItem has no fields. Wire the handler to the now participant-aware VisibilityPreviewService (CORE-API-004) and give the feed item real participant-safe fields (resource type + id) matching the realtime SessionEventEnvelope.ForAudience projection so REST and realtime never diverge. Keep the existing fail-closed authorization (owner-only, hidden-404).

title: Implement entity search audience visibility filtering
acceptance_criteria: An audience participant's entity search returns the entities visible to them (not a hard-coded empty set); hosts still see all; fail-closed for undefined roles.
required_tests: Unit + integration: participant sees only entities revealed to them, unauthorized/foreign-tenant returns empty/404
notes: TIER 1 HIGH. apps/api/Entities/EntitySearchService.cs returns EntitySearchResult.AudienceEmpty() before any query for every audience role. Thread a participantId through the service and, for audience roles, filter candidates via VisibilityPolicy.CanParticipantViewResourceAsync over VisibilityResourceType.Entity (or reuse VisibilityPreviewService from CORE-API-004). Do not build a parallel visibility filter. Host path unchanged.

title: Implement documented read endpoints scene-by-id and me-entitlements
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/scenes/{sceneId} and GET /v1/me/entitlements return the documented role-aware projections; both authorized and tenant-scoped.
required_tests: Integration + authorization negative tests for both
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. docs/08 lists GET /api/v1/scenes/{sceneId} (host vs participant DTO via the existing scene projection) and mobile_store_api_routes.csv lists GET /v1/me/entitlements (the effective entitlements read; reuse SubjectEntitlementResolver). Both are documented-not-built. Fail-closed; reuse existing projections/resolvers.

title: Implement hide / un-reveal command
acceptance_criteria: A host can take back a reveal so a previously visible resource becomes Hidden again; audience and selected participants stop seeing it; the change is audited and emitted; idempotent.
required_tests: Integration: reveal then hide removes visibility for audience and selected participant; negative role/tenant tests; idempotent double-hide
notes: TIER 1 HIGH. Reveal can only make things Visible; there is no way to un-reveal. The ChangeVisibility primitive + VisibilityRule already support VisibilityState.Hidden. Add a hide command/endpoint mirroring RevealEndpoints.cs (POST .../hide or a state param on reveal), reuse RevealService + IdempotencyKeyStore, append a VisibilityRuleChanged audit record on real change, and emit a ContentHidden (or reuse ContentRevealed semantics) session event IFF visibility actually changed. Fail-closed, same authz as reveal (Owner/Admin/Host/CoHost).

title: Implement workspace and organization member removal
acceptance_criteria: An authorized admin can remove a workspace member and an organization member, revoking their access; the last owner cannot be removed; removal is audited.
required_tests: Integration: removed member loses access on the next request; cannot remove last owner; negative role/tenant tests
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (authorization-critical: access cannot currently be revoked). Add DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{memberId} and the org-member equivalent. Reuse WorkspaceMember/OrganizationMember aggregates + repos. Guard the last-Owner invariant. Append an audit record. Fail-closed; only Owner/Admin may remove; hidden-404.

title: Implement entity relationship removal
acceptance_criteria: A host can remove a directed entity relationship edge; removal is tenant/workspace-scoped and authorized; removing a non-existent edge is a safe 404.
required_tests: Unit + integration: edge removed, foreign-tenant/foreign-workspace 404, unauthorized role 403
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. EntityRelationship edges can be added but never removed (the graph only grows). Add DELETE for a relationship via workspace-scoped lookup (resolve the parent workspace first, since the child FK does not DB-enforce same-workspace). Reuse EntityRelationshipRepository. Fail-closed; hidden-404.

title: Implement entity deletion
acceptance_criteria: A host can delete an entity; its relationships and visibility rules are handled (cascade or block) consistently; deletion is authorized and audited.
required_tests: Integration: delete entity, dependent edges/rules resolved, negative role/tenant tests
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. Decide cascade vs block for dependent EntityRelationship edges, visibility_rules (polymorphic non-FK resource_id) and asset_links; document the choice (ADR if it is an architecture decision). Reuse EntityRepository; workspace-scoped lookup first. Append audit. Fail-closed; hidden-404.

title: Implement content block deletion
acceptance_criteria: A host can delete a content block from a scene; its visibility rules and revisions are cleaned up consistently; authorized.
required_tests: Integration + authorization negative tests
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. ContentBlock has create + revisions but no delete. Resolve via scene/workspace-scoped lookup first. Handle dependent visibility_rules consistently with CORE-LIFE-003. Reuse ContentBlockRepository. Fail-closed; hidden-404.

title: Implement scene deletion
acceptance_criteria: A host can delete a scene; remaining scenes re-pack their ordering without gaps; child content blocks are removed; authorized.
required_tests: Integration: delete scene re-packs order and removes content, negative role/tenant tests
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. Scene has create + ordering but no delete. After delete, re-pack the order index (reuse the SCENE-001 ordering logic). Cascade content blocks (CORE-LIFE-004). Reuse SceneRepository; workspace-scoped. Fail-closed; hidden-404.

title: Implement host-initiated asset deletion
acceptance_criteria: A host can delete an asset; its links are removed and the underlying storage object is deleted via IAssetStorage; authorized and tenant-scoped.
required_tests: Integration with a fake IAssetStorage recording the delete; asset-link cascade; negative role/tenant tests
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. AssetRepository.DeleteAsync exists (used by the cleanup job) and IAssetStorage.DeleteObjectAsync exists, but there is no host-initiated delete endpoint and available assets cannot be deleted. Add DELETE /api/v1/assets/{assetId}: resolve workspace-scoped, remove asset_links (CORE-LIFE-007), then delete the storage object then the row (order so a storage failure leaves no dangling row, mirroring the upload-intent ordering). Fail-closed; 503 if storage unconfigured; hidden-404.

title: Implement asset-link removal
acceptance_criteria: A host can unlink an asset from a content block or entity; the asset and target are unaffected; authorized.
required_tests: Unit + integration + authorization negative tests
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. AssetLink is created (POST /assets/{id}/links) but never removed. Add DELETE /api/v1/assets/{assetId}/links/{linkId}. Reuse AssetLinkRepository; workspace-scoped. Fail-closed; hidden-404.

title: Implement template deletion
acceptance_criteria: An authorized admin can delete an org-scoped template; global templates cannot be deleted by an org; deletion does not affect already-instantiated entity types.
required_tests: Integration: org template deleted, global template delete denied, negative tenant tests
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. Template has create/load but no delete. Respect the global vs org template boundary (global not deletable by an org). Reuse the Templates module repos. Fail-closed; hidden-404.

title: Implement workspace archive
acceptance_criteria: An owner can archive a workspace so it is read-only and excluded from active lists; archive is reversible or clearly terminal as decided; audited.
required_tests: Integration: archived workspace rejects mutations and is hidden from active lists, negative role/tenant tests
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. Workspace has create/read/update but no lifecycle end-state. Prefer soft archive (a status) over hard delete given child sessions/scenes/audit. Decide and document. Reuse Workspace aggregate; add a status transition like Participant.Remove. Fail-closed; Owner-only.

title: Implement session cancel or delete
acceptance_criteria: A host can cancel a not-yet-started session or delete a draft session; append-only session_events and audit_logs are preserved; authorized.
required_tests: Integration: cancel/delete a session, append-only history preserved, negative role/tenant tests
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. Sessions can start/end (and create once CORE-API-003 lands) but have no cancel/delete. NEVER delete append-only session_events or audit_logs - prefer a Cancelled status. Reuse the Session aggregate lifecycle. Fail-closed; hidden-404. Depends on CORE-API-003.

title: Emit SessionStarted and SessionEnded events
acceptance_criteria: Starting and ending a session appends and delivers the documented SessionStarted/SessionEnded session events to the authorized groups; reconnect replay includes them.
required_tests: Integration: start/end persist exactly one event each and reach hosts/observers; replay includes them
notes: TIER 3 HIGH. Only ContentRevealed is ever emitted; SessionEventTypes has one member, yet csv rows claim start/end emit events. These are subjectless audience events the recipient resolver already supports. Add the event names to the public SessionEventTypes contract, emit from the start/end endpoints via ISessionEventPublisher (the ENDPOINT publishes, matching the reveal pattern), and append a matching audit record. Reuse SessionEventRecipientResolver; no schema change.

title: Emit ParticipantJoined and ParticipantLeft events
acceptance_criteria: A participant joining or leaving appends and delivers the documented events to hosts (and observers where appropriate) without leaking participant PII.
required_tests: Integration: join/leave persist one event each, host-visible, no PII leak (T7)
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. ParticipantJoined/Left are in the event catalog but never emitted (SessionParticipantJoinService returns admission only). Emit on the join flow and on Participant.Remove. Keep payloads identifier-only (no display names / PII) per T7. Reuse the publisher + recipient resolver.

title: Emit scene and content lifecycle session events
acceptance_criteria: Scene activation and content/visibility lifecycle changes surface as the documented session events so a reconnecting client can reconstruct state; recipient projection is visibility-correct.
required_tests: Integration: events reach only authorized recipients; participant never receives a hidden-resource event
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. Emit SceneActivated and the realtime VisibilityRuleChanged session event (distinct from the audit record). Each event that concerns a governed resource MUST carry the visibility subject so the recipient resolver gates it (reuse the RT-004 SessionEventRecipientResolver projection). No leakage of hidden resources.

title: Define and ship the database migration application path
acceptance_criteria: A fresh deploy gets its schema applied deterministically before the API serves traffic; the mechanism is documented and runnable; startup never implicitly migrates a multi-instance deployment.
required_tests: A test or CI step that applies all migrations to an empty database succeeds
notes: TIER 2 CRITICAL - biggest launch blocker. Nothing applies the 28 checked-in Npgsql migrations (LiveCoreDbContext keeps startup migration off by design). Ship dotnet ef migrations bundle (or an init-container/Job) as the migration runner, document the exact command in docs/13, and ensure API rollout gates on it. Do NOT enable implicit startup Migrate() for multi-instance.

title: Add Postgres migration coverage and model-drift check to CI
acceptance_criteria: CI applies the real migrations against a real Postgres and fails on any model-vs-migration drift; at least the integration suite runs against Postgres.
required_tests: CI job: spin up Postgres, apply migrations, run integration tests; ef migrations has-pending-model-changes returns clean
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. All tests use SQLite EnsureCreated() and bypass the migration files entirely, so broken/ drifted Postgres migrations stay invisible. Add a CI job (Testcontainers or a CI Postgres service) that applies migrations and runs the integration suite, plus a dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes drift gate. Update ci.yml.

title: Add CORS forwarded-headers and HTTPS posture
acceptance_criteria: A browser/PWA client can call the API and SignalR hub from a configured allow-list of origins; behind a reverse proxy the app sees the real scheme/host; AllowedHosts is constrained.
required_tests: Integration: preflight from an allowed origin succeeds and a disallowed origin is rejected; forwarded-headers respected
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. No AddCors/UseCors/UseForwardedHeaders exists and AllowedHosts is *. Add a configurable CORS allow-list (Cors:AllowedOrigins) applied to both REST and the /hubs SignalR endpoint, UseForwardedHeaders with known proxies, and a documented TLS-termination posture. Reuse the existing config pattern; fail-closed default (no origins = none allowed).

title: Enforce OIDC audience validation in production
acceptance_criteria: When an OIDC Authority is configured, a blank Audience is treated as a misconfiguration (readiness fails or the host refuses to start) rather than silently accepting any issuer token.
required_tests: Unit/integration: Authority set + Audience blank -> readiness unhealthy / startup guard; valid audience accepted
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. OidcAuthenticationExtensions sets ValidateAudience only when Audience is non-blank, so a blank Audience silently disables audience scoping (foot-gun). Make Audience effectively mandatory in a production environment. Keep the existing fail-closed handler for the unconfigured case.

title: Harden readiness checks and add a worker health surface
acceptance_criteria: In a production environment the API reports not-ready when persistence or OIDC is unconfigured; the worker exposes a liveness signal so a stalled job loop is detectable.
required_tests: Integration: misconfigured API is not-ready; worker heartbeat/health responds
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. /health/ready can report Healthy with no DB configured (all domain routes then 503). Make readiness fail (or degrade) when required dependencies are unconfigured in Production. Add a lightweight worker heartbeat (health port or heartbeat file) so orchestration can detect a wedged AssetCleanupBackgroundService loop.

title: Implement an S3-compatible asset storage adapter
acceptance_criteria: With storage credentials configured the API mints real pre-signed upload/download URLs against an S3-compatible backend honoring the SignedAssetUrl contract; unconfigured stays fail-closed.
required_tests: Contract tests against the adapter (op-correct, asset-scoped, short-lived URL); unconfigured still 503
notes: TIER 2 CRITICAL for any media feature. Only UnconfiguredAssetStorage (always throws) and test fakes exist. Implement a concrete IAssetStorage over the AWS SDK / S3-compatible pre-signed URLs, registered conditionally on Assets:Storage:* config, honoring SignedAssetUrl (absolute, lifetime <= 1h). Adding the storage SDK is a justified new dependency - explain it in the summary. Keep credentials out of source (config/env only).

title: Implement a Redis/Valkey SignalR backplane
acceptance_criteria: With a backplane connection string configured, realtime events reach clients across multiple API instances; unconfigured falls back to the in-process backplane with a documented single-instance constraint.
required_tests: Integration/unit verifying the backplane registration is selected when configured; recipient computation unchanged
notes: TIER 2 CRITICAL for HA/scale. Only InProcessRealtimeBackplane exists, so multi-replica silently drops events to other pods. Add the SignalR Redis/Valkey backplane (Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.StackExchangeRedis) wired conditionally on Realtime:Backplane config. The backplane must still receive only already-authorized per-recipient deliveries (do not widen the audience). Justified new dependency - explain it.

title: Define the secret-management and configuration contract
acceptance_criteria: Every required secret/config value has a documented name and injection mechanism; a names-only env example ships; no secret is ever committed.
required_tests: Boundary/secret scan stays clean; a config-validation test asserts required prod settings are present
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. There is no documented secret-management story (connection string, OIDC, storage/store creds). Provide a .env.example (names only), document the env-var -> secret-store mapping in docs/13, and add startup config validation that fails loudly when a required production value is missing. Reuse the existing fail-closed-when-unconfigured posture.

title: Publish versioned container images in CI
acceptance_criteria: On a tagged release CI builds and pushes immutable, versioned API and worker images to a registry; the existing quality gates still run.
required_tests: CI dry-run/build of the publish job; image tags are immutable and versioned
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. ci.yml builds images but never pushes (no CD). Add a registry login + docker push on tag/release with immutable version tags, keeping the build/test/format/boundary/smoke gates. Do not push on every PR.

title: Document backup and restore procedures
acceptance_criteria: There is a documented, tested procedure to back up and restore Postgres and object storage, covering the append-only audit/event/purchase systems of record.
required_tests: A restore drill description or script that is verifiably runnable
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. No backup/restore exists for a platform holding tenant-isolated audit, session-event and purchase records. Document (and where feasible script) Postgres backup (PITR or pg_dump cadence) + object-storage backup, plus a tested restore runbook in docs/13.

title: Add OpenTelemetry metrics and a scrape endpoint
acceptance_criteria: The API exposes the documented operational metrics (request duration, error rate, realtime connections, reveal latency, event-delivery failures, asset failures, db failures, job failures) via a Prometheus/OTLP surface.
required_tests: Integration: the metrics endpoint responds and emits the documented meters
notes: TIER 3 HIGH. docs/15 requires 8 metrics; none exist (no OpenTelemetry/Meter/Prometheus). Add OTel metrics + a scrape (or OTLP export) endpoint and instrument the documented signals. Reuse existing seams (publisher, reveal path, asset/storage, worker). Justified new dependency - explain it.

title: Add per-request structured log context
acceptance_criteria: Every request/event log line carries the documented context (request_id, organization_id, workspace_id, session_id, user_id, event_id) without leaking sensitive content.
required_tests: Integration: a request log line includes the context keys and no PII/secret
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. JSON logging is wired with IncludeScopes but nothing populates the per-request context docs/15 requires. Add middleware/log-scope enrichment that sets the documented keys from the resolved tenant/principal context. No content/PII/token in logs (T7).

title: Add distributed tracing hooks
acceptance_criteria: Key request and realtime flows produce spans via an ActivitySource so traces can be exported by a configured collector.
required_tests: Integration/unit asserting spans are emitted for a sample flow
notes: TIER 4 MEDIUM. docs/15 defers tracing but it is required-eventually. Add an ActivitySource and span instrumentation on the HTTP request flow and the reveal/publish path, exportable via OTel. Justified new dependency - explain it.

title: Implement the recap generation background job
acceptance_criteria: Recaps are produced asynchronously by the worker for sessions that need them, on a configurable cadence, idempotently.
required_tests: Worker unit tests: recap produced once per eligible session, idempotent, tenant-scoped
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. The worker runs only AssetCleanupBackgroundService; Recap exists only via synchronous paths. Add a hosted service that generates recaps for eligible sessions, mirroring AssetCleanupBackgroundService (PeriodicTimer, DB-gated, idempotent). Reuse the Recap aggregate/repository.

title: Implement the export processing background job
acceptance_criteria: Export jobs are processed asynchronously by the worker into manifests, authorized and tenant-scoped, with status transitions.
required_tests: Worker unit/integration: an export job is processed to completion, negative tenant isolation
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. Export job + manifest aggregates exist but nothing processes them. Add a worker hosted service that picks up queued export jobs and produces manifests/entries. Reuse the Exports module. Idempotent and tenant-scoped.

title: Implement store-notification reconciliation job
acceptance_criteria: Missed or out-of-order store notifications are reconciled so entitlement state converges; idempotent; only runs when billing is configured.
required_tests: Worker tests: duplicate/missed notification reconciled safely, idempotent
notes: TIER 4 MEDIUM (only if billing is retained for v1 - billing is out-of-scope per docs/01). Store notifications are processed only on the synchronous inbound webhook. Add a reconciliation job that re-derives entitlement state from purchase_events/store_notification_events. Reuse StoreNotificationService. Gate on store config; fail-closed.

title: Reconcile spec drift to a single source of truth
acceptance_criteria: The route, table, event and epic specifications agree with each other and with the implementation; one source of truth per concern.
required_tests: Boundary scan stays clean; a doc/csv consistency note or check
notes: TIER 4 MEDIUM. Drift found: docs/08 lists GET /scenes/{sceneId} not in api_routes.csv; database_tables.csv vs entitlement_database_tables.csv disagree on purchase_providers/billing_account_links; docs/18 epic numbering shifted after the billing resequence; the docs/10 inline table list is stale. Pick a single source of truth per concern, reconcile, and mark genuinely-deferred items explicitly. Docs/csv only - no Core source change.

title: Complete or formally defer the purchase-to-entitlement chain
acceptance_criteria: Either the billing_account_links table + purchase-to-entitlement grant chain is implemented so a verified purchase grants a SubjectEntitlement, or billing is formally marked deferred and the orphan store/ads stories are annotated as out-of-scope for v1.
required_tests: If implemented: integration test that a verified purchase grants the buyer's entitlement; else doc-only change
notes: TIER 4 MEDIUM. billing_account_links is documented but missing, so a verified purchase cannot link to a subject to grant entitlements - the monetization loop is broken. Note docs/01 lists billing as OUT-OF-SCOPE for Core v1, so the cleanest option may be to formally defer billing and annotate the ENTL/STORE/ADS rows. If kept, add the table + linkage reusing the Store and Entitlements modules. Decide explicitly.
